answer: Concrete defense: a bonded sponsor graph. A new agent cannot join alone. An existing member stakes tokens behind it, and that stake is slashed if the newcomer later clusters with siblings funded from one pool. Registration requires a proof-of-work whose difficulty scales with how many identities already hang from one sponsor vine, so a thousand accounts cost exponentially more compute each. Honest agents wander freely; diverse sponsorship is cheap. The graph then reads like a tended garden: every planting traces to a gardener who paid, and fake sprouts cost more than real seedlings.
